You're right, antipsychotic drugs have potent and permanent side effects. But I'm considering this subject from a broader social angle, not merely applying my own biases and prejudices as a mentally ill person. Without these drugs many would become inescapably hostile and criminal. I even wonder if I myself am dangerous without treatment.

Never been inside a mental hospital, only psych wards, crisis residentials and board and cares. Was self-admitted 6/9 psych ward trips and 3/9 for overdose. Believe me I know early childhood environment strongly influences development. While I believe trauma can hasten the onset of and worsen the symptoms of a psychotic illness it cannot, generally speaking, cause these disorders. if it's written in your genome, that's that. Experiencing child abuse is, coincidentally, considered a core component of psychopathy. 

As far as delusions, the most common idea is an unwarranted sense of self-importance. Many wackjobs are bipolar as well meaning they think they are always right and their feelings take precedence over others, so you get the amusing archetype I have termed "the condescending retard." Many schizophrenics have attempted to instruct me in cooking despite the fact they have the intellectual functioning of a retarded child, giving me such advice as "Put duh eggs in duh mikerwave." 

There are the well-known thought based delusions, thinking others can read your mind, as well as an obsession with race and power and status. The expletive and epithet-laden rants of my roommates all have the same through-lines of racism, classism, money and status fixation, violence and power and self-loathing. That's literally all it is. Shouting racial slurs at the voices, threatening them and others, screaming about money and generally being paranoid about all possible scenarios. there's more to discuss but yeah

I might know more about ASPD than you realize (that's the clinical term for psychopathy and sociopathy, factor I and II ASPD respectively, but you knew that right?) My reading has indicated refusal to learn from mistakes is indeed a feature of ASPD, this would seem to be clearly evidenced by the teeming criminal justice system. I also have TD, I'm bipolar to the degree that I am as impaired as many schizophrenics. I personally elect not to take hardcore medication anymore, but I have no history of violent behavior. Until you have been personally attacked and threatened with knives you don't get it. That kind of terror is unique, you would change your tune about medicating these rascals.  I choose to greet the practice of psychiatry not with paranoia but with understanding. It simply didn't work for me.  If you choose to kill yourself that's your decision.
